.qc-cache/hireops-workspace-2026-10-03-r9/rules/harbor-webdev-rubric-qc/references/quality-checks.md section A / '### 1 . instruction_is_a_natural_product_request' (Verify: read instruction.md cold; Defect: numbered acceptance lists, shall/must spec table, feature matrix, or build recipe (framework, file layout, endpoint list)) and adjacent check 4 (runtime contract must be stated)
evidence: Read task/instruction.md cold. It is seven prose paragraphs plus an account line, written first person by a team member: line 1 'Can you build HireOps, the workspace our recruiting team lives in all day? ... so the hard part is that nobody's work gets trampled when someone else acts.'; line 3 'I often move several candidates together; that has to be all of them or none, and I need to be able to undo my last move'; line 5 'Other people's moves should show up on my board within fifteen seconds without a reload, and without closing the card I have open, wiping the note I am typing or moving my cursor.'; line 7 'whether I am reading or halfway through a reply, never touch my draft or my cursor'; line 11 'layout and names are yours. A clear desktop workspace is what matters. We don't need theme switching or a special phone layout.' There are no numbered acceptance lists, no shall/must table, no feature matrix, and no headings or bullets in instruction.md. Requirements are expressed as user needs and pain points (concurrency, undo, live updates, draft preservation, candidate privacy) rather than implementation steps. Build-recipe test (quality-checks.md defect list: framework, file layout, endpoint list): line 13 names Node.js/Express/SQLite, /app/server.js, port 3000/PORT, GET /api/health, /app/app.db/DB_PATH; these are the shared runtime contract that check 4 requires to be stated and that the frozen template integration.md also states verbatim, and the paragraph explicitly disclaims a recipe: 'How you lay the other files and routes out under /app is your call.' Only one endpoint (health) is named; no file layout, schema, component structure or step sequence is prescribed. Line 15 (copy into /app, seed once, persist across restarts) and line 17 (demo accounts) are operational facts a real requester would hand over; demo credentials are an expected house convention per SKILL.md known false positives. Detailed rules are delegated to /instructions/hireops_rules.md (line 11 'The exact stage rules, who may do what, and the conversation rules are in ...'), which is a structured rules note with tables and bullets; that is the template's sanctioned notes location (template notes.md 'write the notes the agent reads under /instructions/'), it reads as an internal team policy doc ('These are the working rules for HireOps, our recruiting workspace... Routes, field names, element ids, button labels and the shape of the pages are yours'), and its voice/structure belongs to row 2/6 rather than this row, which targets the prompt itself. Adversarial attempts: (a) could a reader see line 13 as a recipe? It is a minimal deployment contract, not a build plan, and removing it would create a check-4 defect; (b) could the brief be a checklist disguised as prose? Paragraphs mix motivation ('Several of us have it open at once'), preferences ('dragging is welcome but optional') and scope cuts, which a checklist would not. This row is a source-text judgement; no runtime evidence is required and none was relied on. Minor observation (not a defect): line 13-15 shift to a denser operational register than the rest of the brief, which is typical of a real handoff.
